sources.title: 1860 population census: Spencer Horner household
sources.date: Reference date 1 June 1860; enumeration heading 20 June 1860
sources.provenance: Extracted without alteration from page 1 of the owner-supplied Google Doc export “1860 census,” retrieved 17 October 2026. Heading: Mulberry Township, Johnson County, Arkansas; post office Clarksville. Page No. appears 98, with another handwritten 99; stamped 1029. Dwelling 698, family 699, lines 1–7. NARA series/roll and provider image ID have not been independently reconciled.
sources.supports: Spencer Horner, age 52, farmer, Tennessee; reported real estate $1,500 and personal estate $1,500. Permelia appears on line 2.
sources.limits: Census relationships are not stated in this schedule. Difficult ages and given names require a second reader. Values do not prove cash on hand, total acreage, or an attacker’s motive. Township heading differs from the archive’s earlier Floyd label.
sources.rights: Underlying 1860 federal record; no provider interface is included. Scan provider and reproduction terms still to be recorded.

sources.title: Federal land patent associated with Choctaw Certificate No. 19B
sources.provenance: Existing repository image; original BLM/GLO accession and download provenance need completion.
sources.supports: Spencer Horner as assignee of Co-cha-tubbee, representative of Canne Chubbee, deceased; Choctaw Certificate No. 19B; total 160 acres in sections 19 and 22, T12N R24W. First tract reads SE 1/4 NE 1/4 of section 19.
sources.limits: The patent does not prove Horner’s Indigenous ancestry, the deceased person’s age, the transfer price, or a modern home-site location. First tract corrected from NE 1/4 SE 1/4. The crowded third tract is disputed by a later reader and awaits independent catalog/image comparison; it is not assessed in the lesson. Certificate No. 19B is visible; a catalog accession/patent number is not independently verified.
sources.rights: Underlying federal land patent; retain source identification when reproducing.

sources.title: William Riley Horner marker photograph
sources.date: Marker gives death 10 August 1864; photograph date unknown
sources.provenance: Existing repository screenshot of a marker. Photographer, capture date, marker installation date, and reproduction permission have not been established.
sources.supports: The visible inscription attributes the killing to parties known to his family and gives William’s death date as 10 August 1864.
sources.limits: A memorial is evidence of commemoration. It does not name the killers, establish 2 August as the attack date, prove the date it was installed, or establish whether authorities investigated.
sources.rights: Photograph rights unresolved. Link for study; obtain permission or a new authorized photograph before exhibition or classroom image republication.

sources.title: Family narrative attributed to Eva Horner, 1942
sources.provenance: Published repository excerpts and reconstruction refer to FindAGrave memorial 9297073. The complete dated manuscript and transmission chain remain unverified.
sources.supports: The family account describes Spencer being shot after surrendering, William receiving a head wound, and later reprisals.
sources.limits: The reported seventeen-of-twenty reprisal count, names, tactics, hidden money, and exact chronology are uncorroborated here. Excerpt publication is not a complete diplomatic transcript.
sources.rights: Text permission and original custody unresolved. The optional memory extension uses an attributed editorial summary; core assessment does not depend on it.

sources.title: Henry Stewart entry in Johnson County pension payment ledger
sources.provenance: Existing repository image. Repository/catalog identifier and full ledger title still needed. Filename retained for link compatibility.
sources.supports: An entry for Henry Stewart and pension-payment columns.
sources.limits: This is not a military service card. It does not supply birth in 1840, death in 1930, a unit, or a proven link to the Yale Cemetery individual.

sources.title: GLO compared-copy field notes, T12N R24W
sources.kind: Survey record images and partial transcription
sources.provenance: Arkansas Commissioner of State Lands, Book 913A, bundle BD0164. Retain viewer sequence separately from manuscript page. Images linked in the source folder.
sources.supports: Surveyed fields, streams, roads, and terrain along section lines. Correct readings: Arrington entry 15.00 chains, departure 20.20, river 20.25; Eubanks rather than Subanks.
sources.limits: “G. Homers field” does not establish Spencer’s ownership. A neighboring heading reads 29 December 1843; dating of the continued entry requires adjacent-page review. No precise 1864 event location follows from these notes.
sources.rights: State archive record; confirm COSL reproduction guidance for exhibition facsimiles.

sources.title: Military and pension research leads
sources.provenance: Earlier archive summaries cite William Riley’s Union service/death report, WC75885, John Turner’s rejected application 1,143,763, and Confederate CMSR research. Complete originals not reverified in this release.
sources.supports: Identifies records to retrieve and compare; no new authentication of their quoted contents.
sources.limits: WC75885 concerns William Riley’s widow; it is not John Turner’s rejected application. Sturges authorship/date/context/independence remain open. AWOL status does not locate Hiram Boen or implicate him in killings.
sources.rights: Request repository copies and record-level citations before facsimile publication.
